overview: After 1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3 e6 4.Bg2 Bb4+ Black pins before castling and takes aim at e4 and the White centre. White usually plays 5.Bd2 Be7 (the Alekhine Variation), 5.Nc3 O-O 6.Nh3 or 5.Nd2. Black then plays ...O-O, ...d6, ...Qe8 and ...Qh5 or ...Ne4, aiming for a kingside attack, while White uses the bishop on g2 and a central pawn break e4. Both sides have real winning chances, which makes the line sharp.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, Nh3, O-O and e4 to break the centre
Use the Bg2 on the long diagonal against e6
Gain space with d5 or e4

black_ideas.idea: Build a kingside attack with ...Qh5 and ...Ne4
Control e4 and keep the Dutch structure
